laws.rule: There are laws criminalizing what Russia calls ‘LGBTQIA+ propaganda'. The 'international LGBTQIA+ movement' has been classified as an extremist organisation under Russian law. It is a serious criminal offence to share information or display material promoting 'non-traditional relationships', such as the rainbow flag (including on social media).
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ information

laws.rule: Possessing, selling, consuming, or carrying any illegal drugs is illegal. Penalties are severe and include long prison terms.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Foreigners are required to provide ID in person and confirm their registration on the government services Goslugi Portal (in Russian) or the Unified Biometric System to the mobile network operators to purchase a Russian SIM card. Foreigners and are required to register their International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) against the SIM card with the operator. Foreigners can only use their SIM card with registered mobile equipment. If they change their phone or equipment, they must notify the operator. laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Some Australian documents, such as birth or marriage certificates, need to be legalised before Russian authorities will accept them. If you have an Australian document that you need to use while in Russia, contact the Embassy or Consulate of Russia for information. Apostilles and some legal certificates can be issued by:
laws.heading: Official documents

laws.rule: Russia bans surrogacy for all foreigners except those married to Russian citizens. Recent court cases have resulted in long custodial sentences for some providers of surrogacy services. All children born through surrogacy in Russia are granted Russian citizenship, regardless of their parent's citizenship. Children in these situations will be treated as Russian citizens. Get independent legal advice before making surrogacy arrangements, including with residents of Russia.
laws.heading: Surrogacy laws

laws.rule: Russia has temporarily restricted exporting certain categories of goods, including foreign-made medical products. Russia has strict laws about the import and use of medications, including medications that are available over the counter in Australia, such as cold and flu tablets. When you arrive you must present a doctor's letter to authorities confirming your need for each medication. Especially if your medications contain the following: barbiturate codeine sibutramine anabolic steroids androgens and other sex hormones analgesic, such as tramadol psychostimulants other restricted substances The letter must: contain a description of the medication, including the chemical composition describe
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: Russian Customs provides a list of goods that must be declared when entering or leaving Russia, regardless of whether they come in carry-on or unaccompanied/checked-in luggage. You must declare cash amounts exceeding the equivalent of USD10,000 as well as certain types of goods, including jewellery and antiques. laws.heading: Customs Rules

laws.rule: You should carry an International Driving Permit (IDP). You may drive with an Australian driver's license if you carry it with a notarised Russian translation.
laws.heading: Driving permit

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Smartraveller advises Do not travel. A visa is needed (except on certain commercial cruises); there's no visa on arrival. Australia isn't on the list of countries whose citizens can get Russia's electronic visa, so the visa is applied for through a Russian embassy or consulate.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Consular visa of the correct type (tourist or visitor) through a Russian embassy or consulate.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Apply for the right visa type (fingerprints may be taken), check every detail on the visa before travel (it can't be amended in Russia), and check whether you're on Russia's 'stop list' of Australians denied entry.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: As printed on the visa; some visas, including tourist visas, can't be extended. Stays over 7 working days must be registered.

steps.step: Apply for the correct visa type through a Russian embassy or consulate; Australians can't use the e-visa.
Check the name, passport number, date of birth, visa type, purpose and dates on the visa; return it to the mission for correction if wrong.
On arrival, give biometric data (photo and fingerprints), keep the migration card's exit portion with your passport.
Register a stay of more than 7 working days with the Ministry of Internal Affairs (hotels usually do it; the traveller is responsible) and pay the registration fee.
Leave before the visa expires; overstays bring detention, fines, deportation or bans.

documents: Proof of registration for stays over 7 working days
Customs declaration for cash over USD 10,000
